summary: Pass 52 promotes native.global-world-state from UNKNOWN to STRONG by separating host/imported globals, transient execution scratch, owner-specific Classic gameplay state, and Reforged generic world-state infrastructure. The supplied Worldgroup closure proves all 156 MajorMUD-used symbols are owned and all 34 imported globals/indirects are host runtime/rendering state (32 host_general_runtime, 2 host_message_rendering_transport), so they are not an unidentified MajorMUD gameplay-world-state store. Exact room-action latches and several other gameplay-wide state families already have narrow owners. The generic RuntimeGlobalWorldStateService remains a Reforged shell. Exact unnamed MajorMUD-local record families, remaining bit/mask/counter meanings, full defaults, complete mutation callsites, reset/restart ordering, ordinary persistence mapping, and replication/visibility remain unresolved and fail closed.
classificationPolicy: A shared/global address or generic Reforged state primitive receives no Classic parity credit merely because it exists. Host imported globals are classified at their proven Worldgroup ownership; transient native globals remain execution scratch unless persistence is proven; decoded gameplay state stays with its specific owner. RuntimeGlobalWorldStateService JSON snapshots, reset-policy sorting, revision counters, mutation-source ACLs, value kinds, scopes, and visibility flags are Reforged policy only.

ownerSpecificGameplayState.boundary: Seven shared room/exit latch identities are already assigned to the rooms/living-world authority; the current parity ledger scores native.rooms PASS.
Decoded Classic door definitions have one canonical live state owner; global-world-state does not replace it.
Static placement restoration and maintenance use the recovered limited-item world-plus-owned admission boundary; universal reset ordering remains separate.
MajorMUD Plus contest lifecycle/state is already tracked by its event owner and is STRONG, not assigned to the generic state shell.
NPC respawn admission/Last Killed semantics stay with NPC/living-world timing owners.
WCCMMUD configuration defaults such as KEEPEXP, save clocks, PvP difference and Evil Point settings are configuration evidence, not dynamic generic world-state records.
Reset/maintenance effects are owner-specific and STRONG; exact universal category order remains unresolved.
DFA/Btrieve/MKDE storage ownership is STRONG, but exact mapping of MajorMUD gameplay-world-state record families into Buffer/Player data is still unresolved.
